title: The mycobacterial cell envelope
dek: A covalent AG–mycolate outer membrane, not Gram-positive wallpaper. Almost every first-line drug either builds this sandwich or has to cross it.
story: From cytosol outward: plasma membrane with phosphatidylinositol mannosides and lipoarabinomannan anchors; a peptidoglycan that still uses DAP but with unusual 3-3 cross-links; arabinogalactan covalently tethered to PG; mycolic acids esterified to the AG termini, forming the inner leaflet of an outer membrane; then extractable outer lipids — phthiocerol dimycocerosates (PDIM), sulfoglycolipids, trehalose dimycolate — sitting in the outer leaflet.

That covalent AG–mycolate link is why envelope drugs are not interchangeable. Isoniazid (via InhA) stops meromycolate elongation. Ethambutol hits EmbCAB arabinosyltransferases. Neither is a β-lactam story, and BlaC plus a very different PG make carbapenems a salvage adjunct with clavulanate, not HRZE.

Acid-fastness is a retention assay for carbol fuchsin in this lipid barrier. It is not viability, not species, and not DST. Dead bacilli stain. Nocardia is partially acid-fast. Smear grade is density.
deep: PDIM is required for virulence in several models and for detergent resistance in culture. Some laboratory strains (including some H37Rv stocks) are PDIM-negative; that is a lab-evolution landmine for anyone doing macrophage assays.
Mannose-capped LAM (ManLAM) modulates innate recognition; PILAM of some NTM does not. Do not treat “LAM” as one molecule when you read an immunology paper.
Porin-like systems (MspA in rapid growers; Mtb uses a more limited outer-membrane protein set) and lipid fluidity set the permeability tax that makes gram-negative-style MIC intuition fail.
The envelope is also the staining and the aerosol physics: hydrophobic bacilli ride droplet nuclei. Envelope chemistry is pathogenesis, diagnostics, and drugs in one object.

visual.caption: Outer-in envelope. Extractable virulence lipids sit above the covalent mycolate–AG–PG core. Plasma membrane LAM/PIM and cytoplasm are the floor.
visual.annotation: Acid-fastness lives in the mycolate-rich outer two layers.

example.title: PDIM-negative H37Rv stock
example.setup: A macrophage killing assay with “H37Rv” shows no PDIM peak on TLC. The strain has been passaged on plates for years.

steps.title: Believe the lipid
steps.body: Laboratory MTBC loses PDIM readily. Your virulence phenotype may be a stock artefact.

steps.title: Check the genome
steps.body: Frameshifts in pps/mas/fadD26 are common. WGS of the working stock is part of the methods.

steps.title: Do not compare to clinical L2
steps.body: A PDIM-null lab strain is not a surrogate for a cavitary isolate’s envelope.

example.takeaway: The envelope is a phenotype you can lose in the freezer.

check.prompt: Ethambutol’s primary biosynthetic target in the envelope is:
check.why: EMB is an AG drug. InhA is INH/ETH. GyrA is FQ. AtpE is BDQ.

check.prompt: Order these from outside to cytoplasm: (1) peptidoglycan (2) extractable PDIM/TDM (3) AG-linked mycolates (4) plasma membrane. Which sequence is correct?
check.why: Extractable lipids, then mycolate OM, then AG/PG core, then membrane. The covalent mycolates sit outside PG.

whyWrong.1-3-2-4: PG is not the outermost layer.
whyWrong.2-1-3-4: Mycolates are outside PG, not under it.
